tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A parent wants a government-backed savings scheme for the education and marriage of a girl child under ten years of age. The most suitable scheme is the:
options: Sukanya Samriddhi Account at a post office or an authorised bank
Kisan Vikas Patra meant for the farmers only
Senior Citizens Savings Scheme at a post office
National Savings Certificate for the women above 60 years

questions.question_text: A Sukanya Samriddhi Account can be opened in the name of a girl child who is below the age of:
options: 14 years
18 years
10 years
21 years

questions.question_text: In a Sukanya Samriddhi Account, deposits have to be made for:
options: 10 years from the date of opening the account
21 years from the date of opening the account
15 years from the date of opening the account
5 years from the date of opening the account

questions.question_text: The Sukanya Samriddhi Account matures after:
options: 25 years from the date of opening the account
15 years from the date of opening the account
21 years from the date of opening the account
18 years from the date of opening the account

questions.question_text: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) account has a lock-in or maturity period of:
options: 25 years, not extendable at any time
10 years, extendable in blocks of two years
15 years, extendable in blocks of five years
5 years, extendable in blocks of one year

questions.question_text: The maximum amount that can be deposited in a PPF account in a financial year is:
options: Rs 1 lakh
Rs 5 lakh
Rs 1.5 lakh
Rs 2.5 lakh

questions.question_text: The minimum annual deposit required to keep a PPF account active is:
options: Rs 100
Rs 500

questions.question_text: PPF is called an EEE instrument because, under the old regime:
options: Only the interest is exempt while the deposit and maturity are taxed
The deposit is exempt but both the interest and the maturity are taxed
Only the deposit is exempt while the interest and maturity are taxed
The deposit, the interest and the maturity amount are all tax-exempt

questions.question_text: Partial withdrawal from a PPF account is permitted from:
options: The third financial year after the year of opening the account
The first financial year after the year of opening the account
The seventh financial year after the year of opening the account
The fifteenth financial year after the year of opening the account

questions.question_text: A loan against the PPF balance is available from the:
options: Third financial year up to the sixth financial year
Seventh financial year up to the fifteenth financial year
First financial year up to the second financial year
Tenth financial year up to the fifteenth financial year

questions.question_text: The interest rate on the PPF is:
options: Linked to the Sensex and changes every day
Fixed by each bank for its own customers
Fixed at 12% for all the years
Fixed by the government and reviewed every quarter

questions.question_text: The rule on opening a PPF account is that a person can have:
options: Any number of accounts in his own name at the post offices
Two accounts in his own name at the private sector banks
One joint account with his spouse at a cooperative bank
One account in his own name at a post office or an authorised bank

questions.question_text: A PPF account cannot be opened:
options: By an adult resident individual
At an authorised public sector bank
In the name of a Hindu undivided family
By a guardian for a minor

questions.question_text: A person deposits Rs 1,50,000 every year in PPF at an assumed 7% compounded annually. Which is the correct statement about the maturity value after 15 years?
options: It is exactly Rs 45 lakh, being double of the total deposits
It is equal to Rs 22.5 lakh, the total of deposits, as interest is not paid
It is less than Rs 22.5 lakh, the total of deposits, due to the tax
It is more than Rs 22.5 lakh, the total of deposits, because of the interest

questions.question_text: The National Savings Certificate (NSC) has a maturity period of:
options: 3 years
10 years
5 years
15 years

questions.question_text: The interest on the NSC is:
options: Paid quarterly in the form of cheques
Paid weekly into the savings account
Paid monthly into the account of the holder
Compounded annually but paid at the maturity

questions.question_text: The Kisan Vikas Patra is a scheme in which the invested amount:
options: Is repaid only after the death of the holder
Is converted into the shares of a company
Doubles in a fixed period at the notified rate
Is lost if the market falls

questions.question_text: The Senior Citizens Savings Scheme is open to persons who are:
options: Below 18 years of age, through their guardians at the bank
Of any age, provided they deposit at least Rs 10 lakh
Aged 45 years or above, with no exception at all for anyone
Aged 60 years or above, with relaxed conditions for early retirees

questions.question_text: The maximum investment limit in the SCSS per person is:
options: Rs 5 lakh
Rs 30 lakh
Rs 1 crore
Rs 15 lakh

questions.question_text: The interest on the SCSS is paid:
options: At the maturity only
Quarterly
Annually
Every day

questions.question_text: The Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS) is meant for those who want:
options: A regular monthly income from the invested lump sum
A loan against the property
A tax-free lump sum on the retirement
Insurance against the death

questions.question_text: A Post Office Savings Account differs from a bank savings account in that it:
options: Does not pay any interest to the holder of the account
Is operated through a post office, though cheque and ATM facilities now exist
Is available only to the employees of the government
Cannot be opened by an individual in his own name at all

questions.question_text: A Post Office Recurring Deposit requires the depositor to:
options: Deposit only on the festival days of the year in a given month
Deposit a lump sum once at the start and leave it for five years
Deposit a fixed amount every year for a period of fifteen years
Deposit a fixed amount every month for a period of five years

questions.question_text: A Post Office Time Deposit is similar to:
options: A demand draft issued for the payment to a supplier
A credit card issued by a bank to its good customers
A bank current account kept by the traders for daily use
A bank fixed deposit with a tenure of 1, 2, 3 or 5 years

questions.question_text: India Post Payments Bank is meant to provide:
options: Stock broking services to the investors in the share market
Basic banking, payments and doorstep services through the postal staff
Large corporate loans running into the crores of rupees
Foreign exchange services to the importers and the exporters

tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: The EPF contribution by an employee and employer is generally what percentage of the basic pay plus dearness allowance?
options: 8% and 12% respectively
5% each
12% each
10% each

questions.question_text: An employee's basic pay plus DA is Rs 30,000 per month. The total EPF contribution of the employee and the employer (12% each) in a month is:
Of the employer's 12% contribution to the EPF, the share that goes to the Employees' Pension Scheme is:
options: The whole 12% without any ceiling
3.67% of the basic pay and DA only
8.33%, subject to the wage ceiling
Nil, as the pension is paid by the government

questions.question_text: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation is a:
options: Private company working in the corporate sector of the country
Department of the Reserve Bank of India for the pension schemes
Statutory body working under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
Wing of the post office department for the savings schemes

questions.question_text: The Universal Account Number (UAN) is:
options: A unique 12-digit number given to each EPF member
A bank account number for the salaried persons
A number of the insurance policy
A tax number issued by the income tax department

questions.question_text: A person who changes jobs can retain the EPF benefits by:
options: Transferring the account to the new employer under the same UAN
Withdrawing and spending the whole of the amount in the account
Opening a new account every time he joins a new employer
Closing his UAN and asking for a new one at each employer

questions.question_text: Withdrawal of the EPF before five years of continuous service may attract:
options: Income tax or TDS on the withdrawal under certain conditions
A bonus from the government for withdrawing early
No consequence whatever, as it is the employee's own money
A penalty on the employer alone, and not on the member

questions.question_text: The Voluntary Provident Fund allows an employee to:
options: Withdraw at any time without tax and without any condition
Contribute only through the employer with its consent
Reduce the contribution to below 12% of the basic pay
Contribute more than 12% of the basic pay at the same interest rate

questions.question_text: The National Pension System (NPS) is regulated by the:
options: Reserve Bank of India
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
Securities and Exchange Board of India
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority

questions.question_text: The NPS Tier I account is:
options: A voluntary savings account with free withdrawals at any time
The main pension account, with restrictions on withdrawal
A foreign currency account meant for the non-resident Indians
A current account meant for the traders and the businessmen

questions.question_text: The NPS Tier II account is:
options: A tax-saving account with the highest deduction in the NPS
A compulsory account with a lock-in of till the age of 60 years
A loan account of the NPS to be given for the housing needs
A voluntary savings account with no lock-in, opened along with Tier I

questions.question_text: At the age of 60, an NPS subscriber is required to use at least what share of the corpus to buy an annuity?
questions.explanation: The rest, up to 60%, can be taken as a lump sum.

questions.question_text: On exit at 60 from the NPS, the maximum lump sum that can be withdrawn is:
options: 40% of the corpus
60% of the corpus
20% of the corpus
100% of the corpus

questions.question_text: The Atal Pension Yojana is aimed at:
options: Giving small loans to the shopkeepers in the small towns
Giving a lump sum on death to the farmers in the villages
Giving a fixed monthly pension to workers in the unorganised sector
Giving a tax refund to the salaried persons in the cities

questions.question_text: Under the APY, the guaranteed monthly pension after the age of 60 ranges from:
options: Rs 500 to Rs 1,000

questions.question_text: The eligible age for joining the APY is:
options: 21 to 35 years
18 to 60 years
18 to 40 years
25 to 65 years

questions.question_text: An annuity is:
options: A lump sum payment received only once at the time of the maturity
A loan taken against the security of the pension of the person
A series of regular payments received for a given period or for life
A tax deducted at source on the pension received by the person

questions.question_text: Gratuity is a benefit payable by an employer under the:
options: Minimum Wages Act, 1948
Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
Factories Act, 1948

questions.question_text: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, the minimum years of continuous service for eligibility are generally:
options: Five years
Fifteen years
Ten years
One year

questions.question_text: Gratuity = (last drawn salary × 15 × years of service)/26. For a salary of Rs 26,000 and 10 years of service, the gratuity is:
Income tax in India is levied on the income of a:
options: Current year, in the same year of earning
Future year, as forecast
Previous year, in the assessment year that follows
Next year, in the year before earning

questions.question_text: For the income earned during the financial year 2024-25, the assessment year is:
The Permanent Account Number (PAN) consists of:
options: 10 alphanumeric characters
12 numeric digits
16 numeric digits
8 alphabetic characters

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the heads of income under the Income-tax Act?
options: Income from house property
Wages paid to casual labourers in a factory
Capital gains
Income from salary
questions.explanation: Heads: salary, house property, business/profession, capital gains, other sources.

questions.question_text: The five heads of income under the Income-tax Act are:
options: Salary, profit, loss, tax and cess of the person in the year
Salary, wages, rent, interest and dividend income of the person
Agriculture, industry, services, trade and commerce income
Salary, house property, business or profession, capital gains, other sources

tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: Agricultural income in India is:
options: Taxable only if it is earned by a company in the year
Exempt from the central income tax, but may be considered for the rate purposes
Fully taxable at the highest slab rate of the income tax
Taxable only in the first year of the earning of the income

questions.question_text: An individual who is below 60 years of age and is a resident is classified as a:
options: Senior citizen under the tax law
Super senior citizen under the tax law
Non-resident Indian under the tax law
Resident individual (non-senior citizen)

questions.question_text: A "senior citizen" for the income-tax purposes is an individual resident aged:
options: 50 years or more but less than 70 years
65 years or more but less than 90 years
60 years or more but less than 80 years
80 years or more

questions.question_text: A "super senior citizen" is an individual aged:
options: 80 years or more
60 years or more
90 years or more
70 years or more

questions.question_text: A person is a resident in India for tax purposes if he stays in India for at least:
options: 365 days in the previous year, with no other condition at all
182 days in the previous year, or meets the other prescribed conditions
60 days in the previous year, with no other condition at all
90 days in the previous year, with no other condition at all

questions.question_text: The tax-saving deduction of up to Rs 1.5 lakh under the old regime is allowed under:
options: Section 80G
Section 80C
Section 80D
Section 24

questions.question_text: An investment that qualifies for deduction under Section 80C of the old regime is:
options: Shares bought on the stock exchange for short-term trading
PPF, ELSS mutual funds or a tax-saving fixed deposit
Gold coins bought for making the jewellery of the family
A savings bank account with a balance of Rs 1.5 lakh

questions.question_text: Section 80D of the Income-tax Act provides the deduction for:
options: The premium paid for the health insurance
The contribution to the political parties
The interest on the education loan
The donations to the charitable institutions

questions.question_text: The deduction for donations to charitable institutions is available under:
options: Section 80G
Section 80C
Section 80D
Section 24

questions.question_text: The interest on the housing loan on a self-occupied property is deductible under the old regime up to Rs 2 lakh under:
options: Section 24(b)
Section 80C
Section 80D
Section 80G

questions.question_text: The standard deduction for salaried employees is:
options: The amount of the donations made in the year by the employee
The actual amount spent on the clothing for the office
The amount of the tax paid in the previous year by the employee
A flat amount deducted from the salary income without any proof

questions.question_text: House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption is based on the least of the actual HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of the salary, and a percentage of the salary. This is meant to:
options: Tax the rent received by the landlord
Exempt the whole salary of the employee
Reduce the taxable salary of an employee who pays rent
Increase the taxable salary of the employee

questions.question_text: TDS on salary is deducted by the employer under:
options: Section 194C
Section 195
Section 192
Section 194A

questions.question_text: Form 16 is a certificate issued by the:
options: Bank, giving the details of the account balance
Employer, giving the details of the TDS on salary
Stock broker, giving the details of the trades
Insurance company, giving the details of the premium

questions.question_text: Form 26AS or the annual information statement shows:
options: The premium paid on the life insurance policies of the taxpayer
The balance lying in the bank account of the taxpayer at the year end
The loans that have been taken by the taxpayer from the lenders
The tax deducted or collected on behalf of the taxpayer and other details

questions.question_text: An Income Tax Return is filed in order to:
options: Apply for a PAN card from the income tax department
Get a loan sanctioned automatically from a bank or NBFC
Open a bank account in the name of the person for salary
Report the income and tax paid and claim the refund, if any

questions.question_text: The ITR form for a salaried individual with a salary and one house property and a small interest income is generally:
options: ITR-7
ITR-3
ITR-5
ITR-1 (Sahaj)

questions.question_text: The due date for filing the ITR for a non-audit individual taxpayer is generally:
options: 31 July of the assessment year
31 December of the assessment year
30 April of the assessment year
31 March of the assessment year

questions.question_text: A belated return can be filed on payment of a late fee:
options: Under Section 234F, up to the date prescribed
Only by the companies
Without any condition at any time
Only for the previous three years

questions.question_text: Advance tax is payable by an assessee whose estimated tax liability for the year is:
options: Rs 1,000 or more
Rs 50,000 or more
Rs 1 lakh or more
Rs 10,000 or more

questions.question_text: Interest on a savings bank account is taxable under the head:
options: Income from salary, as it is earned by an employee
Income from business or profession, as it is a business receipt
Income from other sources, with a limited deduction under Section 80TTA
Income from house property, as it is earned by an owner

questions.question_text: The deduction under Section 80TTA for savings account interest (for non-senior individuals) is up to:
options: Rs 1 lakh

questions.question_text: The deduction under Section 80TTB for senior citizens on the interest from deposits is up to:
options: Rs 1 lakh

questions.question_text: Long-term capital gains on listed equity shares held for more than 12 months are taxed:
options: At the normal slab rate of the person, with no exemption at all
At a concessional special rate, subject to the specified exemption limit
At 0% in every case, whatever may be the amount of the gain
At 100% of the gain, as no cost of acquisition is allowed

questions.question_text: A capital asset such as a house sold after holding for more than 24 months gives:
options: A long-term capital gain
A short-term capital gain
A business income
A salary income

tests.title: Unit 4: Financial Services from Post Office, Provident and Pension Funds, Tax – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: GST is best described as a:
options: Tax on the foreign exchange that is bought by the individuals
Direct tax on the income earned by the individuals each year
Destination-based indirect tax on the supply of goods and services
Tax on the property which is owned by the individuals each year

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an indirect tax?
options: Capital gains tax
Wealth tax
Income tax
GST

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a direct tax?
options: Customs duty
Income tax
Excise duty
GST
questions.explanation: Paid by the person on whom it is levied.

questions.question_text: The burden of an indirect tax can be:
options: Shifted to the consumers by the sellers
Shifted to the government by the consumers
Not shifted at all
Shifted to the banks by the sellers

questions.question_text: A cess is:
options: A loan taken by the government from the public for its needs
A fine imposed by the government on a violation of a law
A fee charged by the government for a particular service rendered
A tax levied for a specific purpose, over and above the basic tax

questions.question_text: Health and education cess on income tax is charged at:
options: 4% of the income tax plus surcharge
10% of the total income
20% of the tax
1% of the income

questions.question_text: A surcharge on income tax is:
options: A subsidy given to the low income earners
A tax on the foreign income of the residents only
An additional tax on the high income earners
A refund given to the senior citizens

questions.question_text: The Section 87A rebate in income tax:
options: Reduces or removes the tax for resident individuals up to a specified income
Applies only to the non-resident individuals who live abroad
Applies only to the individuals earning above Rs 1 crore
Applies only to the companies and the firms registered in India

questions.question_text: Under the new tax regime, most of the exemptions and deductions such as 80C and HRA are:
options: Not available, with the lower slab rates in return
Available only for the senior citizens
Available only for the companies
Available in full, with the higher rates

questions.question_text: A taxpayer chooses between the old and the new regime by comparing:
options: Only the rate of tax in the first slab of each of the regimes
Only the amount of the HRA exemption in each of the regimes
Only the amount of the standard deduction in each regime
The total tax payable under each regime after counting the deductions

questions.question_text: Tax evasion differs from tax avoidance in that evasion is:
options: Illegal concealment of the income or the false claims
Legal use of the provisions to reduce the tax
Payment of the tax on time
Filing of the return on time

questions.question_text: Tax planning means:
options: Arranging the affairs legally to minimise the tax
Hiding the income from the department
Not filing the return
Paying the tax late

questions.question_text: If excess tax has been paid or deducted, the taxpayer can claim:
options: A loan from the department
A refund by filing the return
A subsidy from the bank
A penalty from the employer

questions.question_text: TDS on interest from a bank fixed deposit is deducted under:
options: Section 192, as it is the same as the TDS on salary
Section 194C, as it is the same as the TDS on contracts
Section 194A when the interest exceeds the prescribed limit
Section 195, as it is the same as the TDS on foreign payments

questions.question_text: If a deductee does not quote the PAN, the TDS rate can be:
options: Lower than the normal rate, to encourage the filing of returns
Zero, as the department cannot trace the person without a PAN
Reduced to half, for the first year of such non-quoting
Higher, at 20% or the rate in force, whichever is higher

questions.question_text: The Aadhaar and the PAN are required to be:
options: Surrendered by the holder on attaining the age of sixty years
Linked, failing which the PAN may become inoperative
Exchanged between the banks every year for the verification
Kept separate always, as the law does not allow the linking

questions.question_text: The Income-tax Act requires furnishing of the PAN while opening a bank account except in the case of:
options: The women only
Persons without a PAN, who may furnish Form 60
The senior citizens only
The persons with the income above Rs 10 lakh

questions.question_text: The Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN) has:
options: 8 characters
10 characters
12 characters
15 characters

questions.question_text: Under GST, the composition scheme is available to:
options: Banks and insurance companies registered in the country
Small taxpayers whose turnover is up to a prescribed limit
Companies having a turnover above Rs 100 crore a year
Large exporters of goods and services across the countries

questions.question_text: The input tax credit under GST allows a registered person to:
options: Set off the tax paid on inputs against the tax payable on outputs
Avoid the tax on the output sold to the final consumers
Claim a refund of the income tax paid in the earlier years
Pay no tax at all on the purchases made for the business

questions.question_text: A trader collects Rs 18,000 as GST on sales and has paid Rs 12,000 as GST on the purchases. The GST payable is:
The tax-saving fixed deposit under Section 80C has a lock-in period of:
options: 5 years
1 year
3 years
10 years

questions.question_text: The ELSS (equity-linked savings scheme) has a lock-in period of:
options: 3 years
5 years
1 year
7 years

questions.question_text: A salaried person invests Rs 1,50,000 in 80C-eligible schemes under the old regime and is in the 20% tax bracket. The approximate tax saved (ignoring the cess) is:
The BEST reason for filing the ITR even when the income is below the taxable limit is that it:
options: Leads to the payment of an additional tax on the small income
Helps in claiming refunds and is a proof of income for loans and visas
Is a legal bar to the opening of a bank account in the name
Reduces the amount of income of the person for the next year
